case_title: RAM AUTAR & ORS. v. STATE OF U.P.
high_court_outcome: Modified conviction to one under Section 304 Part I
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were relatives with a common ancestor. The incident began when the victim's cattle strayed into the fields of the accused and destroyed crops, leading to abuse from the accused. Later, an altercation occurred between the victim and the accused while they were sitting in their compounds. The accused, under exhortation, brought a gun and fired at the victim, who was then assaulted with lathis. The victim died on the spot. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts and medical evidence showing the victim had firearm wounds and other injuries, while the accused also had minor injuries. The High Court concluded that the accused did not have a criminal background and that the incident occurred without premeditation, leading to a conviction under Section 304 Part I with a reduced sentence.
